pair: zero-scan bound (handleUdpFrame_*)
esp32_behaviour: Zero-scan loop bound is `i + 1 < packetSize`, so the last in-bounds pair read is (packetSize-2, packetSize-1); never reads index packetSize (src/esp32/udp_frame_esp32.cpp:51).
nrf52_behaviour: FIXED (BUG-13 follow-up, commit cd88ae12 applied the ESP32 bound to nRF52 too): now reads the identical bound `i + 1 < packetSize` (src/nrf52/udp_frame_nrf52.cpp:53). Previously read `i < packetSize`, one byte past the datagram on odd packetSize, which could flip the accept/reject verdict.
evidence: test/test_udp_frame_twin/test_udp_frame_twin.cpp:613-659 (test_agreement_zero_scan_bound_matches_on_odd_length, now an AGREEMENT case, not drift) and :661-704 (test_regression_zero_scan_oob_byte_flips_verdict_before_fix, permanent regression pin)
recommendation: Already fixed on nRF52 to match ESP32's bound; no further action. Keep the regression test as the permanent guard against reintroducing the one-byte over-read. FIXED: nRF52 now uses the same in-bounds scan as ESP32 (src/nrf52/udp_frame_nrf52.cpp:53); the two sides no longer disagree on this bound.

pair: RX-01 unconfigured-source guard, inbound GATE frame (first door, server-RX path)
esp32_behaviour: A GATE frame whose decoded APRS source call is still the factory default (isUnconfiguredCall()) is counted via logRxDropUnconfigured() and refused relay to the LoRa TX ring; its debug print is suppressed (src/esp32/udp_frame_esp32.cpp:122-130, :148).
nrf52_behaviour: No such check exists in handleUdpFrame_nrf52() -- an unconfigured-source GATE frame decodes, prints and relays exactly like any other (absent anywhere between the decode at src/nrf52/udp_frame_nrf52.cpp:119 and the dedup/relay block at :286-335).
evidence: test/test_udp_frame_twin/test_udp_frame_twin.cpp:907-936 (test_drift_rx01_unconfigured_guard_esp32_only)
recommendation: Port the RX-01 guard to handleUdpFrame_nrf52(): an unconfigured-source frame relayed onto LoRa by an nRF52 gateway defeats the primary OnRxDone guard's purpose (BACKLOG 3.8k).

pair: hb_warn_logged reset discipline
esp32_behaviour: hb_warn_logged is reset to false in all four branches of handleUdpFrame_esp32() that indicate live server traffic: GATE text/pos/hey (:103), CONF (:366), BEAT (:456), unrecognised/OTHER (:464); consumed by the WiFi heartbeat-staleness diagnostic in gatewayService_esp32() (src/esp32/gateway_service_esp32.cpp:36-49).
nrf52_behaviour: hb_warn_logged does not exist on nRF52 at all -- grep across src/ finds it only in esp32/udp_frame_esp32.cpp, esp32/gateway_service_esp32.cpp, esp32/esp32_main.cpp and its declaration site loop_functions.cpp:554; handleUdpFrame_nrf52() has no equivalent reset anywhere.
evidence: src/esp32/udp_frame_esp32.cpp:103,366,456,464 vs. absence in src/nrf52/udp_frame_nrf52.cpp (grep, no match). No U1 twin case exercises this directly -- the twin stubs out gatewayService_esp32(), so this row is source-sourced, not test-sourced.
recommendation: hb_warn_logged backs an ESP32-only WiFi-connectivity diagnostic (gatewayService_esp32()); nRF52's Ethernet link has its own, structurally different recovery path (see DR-15). Decide whether nRF52 needs the same diagnostic before porting the flag 1:1, or whether DR-15's recovery already covers the same case by a different route.

pair: bGATEWAY_NOPOS veto on relaying a UDP position frame
esp32_behaviour: In the position branch (msg_type_b==0x21): `if(bGATEWAY_NOPOS) bUDPtoLoraSend=false;` vetoes the relay (src/esp32/udp_frame_esp32.cpp:176-177); bGATEWAY_NOPOS is set from meshcom_settings.node_sset2 & 0x0100 in esp32_main.cpp:853.
nrf52_behaviour: handleUdpFrame_nrf52() never references bGATEWAY_NOPOS (grep over src/nrf52/udp_frame_nrf52.cpp: no match), even though nrf52_main.cpp:582 sets the identical flag from the identical settings bit -- the setting exists and is honoured elsewhere but not read at the one place that would apply it to a relayed UDP position frame.
evidence: test/test_udp_frame_twin/test_udp_frame_twin.cpp:821-884 (test_drift_dedup_gate_position_esp32_honors_gateway_nopos_nrf52_does_not, drift half at :864-884)
recommendation: Port the bGATEWAY_NOPOS check into handleUdpFrame_nrf52()'s position branch; the setting is already computed and available, only the read is missing.

pair: sendDisplayPosition() call and TM-31 early-dedup insert for a relayed position frame
esp32_behaviour: Calls sendDisplayPosition(aprsmsg, 99, 0) for msg_type_b==0x21 (src/esp32/udp_frame_esp32.cpp:170) and reads the dedup gate is_new_packet() BEFORE inserting this msg_id via addLoraRxBuffer() in the same branch (:140-146, :173) -- the documented TM-31 fix (comment :132-139).
nrf52_behaviour: Never calls sendDisplayPosition() anywhere in handleUdpFrame_nrf52() (only sendDisplayText(), :183/:188/:259); the dedup read (is_new_packet(), :294) happens once, after the position branch, with no early/duplicate insert to begin with -- the historical TM-31 self-dedup symptom does not reproduce on either side today, but the code shape still differs.
evidence: test/test_udp_frame_twin/test_udp_frame_twin.cpp:886-905 (test_drift_senddisplayposition_esp32_only); TM-31 structural note at :821-838, agreement half at :843-862 shows the historical bug is gone on both sides
recommendation: Port sendDisplayPosition() to the nRF52 position branch if the on-device/BLE display update is wanted there too. The TM-31 early-dedup structural difference is now a no-op difference (neither side exhibits the original bug) and can be unified for code hygiene without behaviour risk.

pair: decodeAPRS() return-value check
esp32_behaviour: Calls decodeAPRS(convBuffer, lora_tx_msg_len, aprsmsg) and discards the return value -- proceeds to build source_call/destination_call and continues processing regardless of whether decode recognised the frame (src/esp32/udp_frame_esp32.cpp:117-120).
nrf52_behaviour: Captures the return into msg_type_b_lora and gates all further processing on `if(msg_type_b_lora > 0)` (src/nrf52/udp_frame_nrf52.cpp:119-121) -- an unrecognised/malformed frame is not processed further.
evidence: src/esp32/udp_frame_esp32.cpp:117 vs. src/nrf52/udp_frame_nrf52.cpp:119-121. Not a dedicated drift case in test_udp_frame_twin -- every corpus frame in that suite is well-formed and decodes on both sides, so this row is source-sourced, not twin-sourced.
recommendation: Port nRF52's return-value check to ESP32: proceeding with an aprsMessage that decodeAPRS() did not populate is a correctness risk (garbage source_call/destination_call feeding the relay/ACK/CONF logic below).

pair: sendExtern() precondition gate (inbound GATE frame)
esp32_behaviour: Forwards to EXTUDP only when hasExternIPaddress is true, and only then checks bEXTUDP (src/esp32/udp_frame_esp32.cpp:108-112).
nrf52_behaviour: Forwards on bEXTUDP alone (src/nrf52/udp_frame_nrf52.cpp:98-99); hasExternIPaddress is never referenced anywhere in the file.
evidence: test/test_udp_frame_twin/test_udp_frame_twin.cpp:710-736 (test_drift_extudp_requires_hasExternIPaddress_on_esp32_only)
recommendation: Port the hasExternIPaddress gate to nRF52; forwarding to an unresolved/absent extern destination is at best wasted work and at worst a misdirected send once nRF52 gains its own extern-IP concept.

pair: CONF-frame source-match guard, zero-address case
esp32_behaviour: Rejects if `(uint32_t)node_hostip == 0 || src_ip != node_hostip` -- an explicit, independent check that the gateway address has actually resolved, in addition to the source match (src/esp32/udp_frame_esp32.cpp:381-385).
nrf52_behaviour: Rejects only on `!(remote_ip == neth.udp_dest_addr)` (src/nrf52/udp_frame_nrf52.cpp:372-377) -- no separate zero-address check; if neth.udp_dest_addr is still 0.0.0.0 (pre-DHCP/pre-resolve), a CONF datagram whose source reads as 0.0.0.0 would pass the equality check that ESP32's explicit zero-guard exists specifically to catch.
evidence: src/esp32/udp_frame_esp32.cpp:369-385 (comment explains the guard's intent) vs. src/nrf52/udp_frame_nrf52.cpp:359-377. Not a dedicated drift case in test_udp_frame_twin -- test_agreement_conf_updates_node_call_and_short_identically (:565-611) only exercises a spoofed non-zero mismatched source, not the zero-address edge case.
recommendation: Port the explicit zero-address check to nRF52's CONF guard; the ESP32 comment (:369-380) treats it as a deliberate anti-spoofing measure, not an accident.

pair: ACK phone-frame (BLE) construction on receipt of a UDP :ack/:rej text
esp32_behaviour: Builds via buildAckPhoneFrame() (src/ack_attribution.h:122-138), which appends the acknowledging callsign as a variable-length suffix (base 7 bytes + up to 10 attribution bytes) and forwards the real length: addBLEOutBuffer(print_buff, plen) (src/esp32/udp_frame_esp32.cpp:253-258).
nrf52_behaviour: Builds the 7-byte base frame by hand inline (src/nrf52/udp_frame_nrf52.cpp:215-223) and always calls addBLEOutBuffer(print_buff, 7) (:242) -- no call-attribution suffix is ever attached. Note: the ACK-status byte itself (print_buff[5]) was already brought in line with ESP32 by the DRY-21 fix noted in the same file (:229-234); only the length/attribution part of this row remains open.
evidence: src/ack_attribution.h:122-138; src/esp32/udp_frame_esp32.cpp:253,258; src/nrf52/udp_frame_nrf52.cpp:217-223,242. Not a case in test_udp_frame_twin (neither handler's corpus frame contains an :ack/:rej payload) -- source-sourced.
recommendation: Switch nRF52 to buildAckPhoneFrame() so the app gets call attribution from nRF52 gateways too, same as ESP32; DRY-21 already closed the ACK-status-byte half of this gap, this closes the rest.

pair: msg_buffer storage class in checkSerialCommand()
esp32_behaviour: `char msg_buffer[600];` is a plain function-local (stack) (src/esp32/serial_command_esp32.cpp:111).
nrf52_behaviour: `static char msg_buffer[600];` (BSS), changed by N-22 as a loop-task stack-usage fix (src/nrf52/serial_command_nrf52.cpp:90).
evidence: test/test_serial_command_twin/test_serial_command_twin.cpp:399-425 (test_stale_buffer_content_does_not_leak_between_calls) -- the test's own comment concludes the storage-class change is NOT behaviourally observable from outside (both sides NUL-terminate at the same point); the only evidence for 'why it matters' is N-22's motivation (nRF52 loop-task stack pressure), not an observed symptom.
recommendation: Same N-22 rationale (stack-usage headroom) likely applies to ESP32's loop task too, just not yet forced by an observed overflow; recommend moving ESP32's copy to static/file-scope as a preventive match rather than waiting for an ESP32 stack-overflow incident.

pair: net-console (Telnet/TCP) input source in checkSerialCommand()
esp32_behaviour: Reads netConsoleAvailable()/netConsoleRead() as a second input source alongside Serial, including a telnet IAC-negotiation skip (src/esp32/serial_command_esp32.cpp:58-66 and following).
nrf52_behaviour: No net-console code at all -- neither function is called anywhere in serial_command_nrf52.cpp (grep, no match).
evidence: test/test_serial_command_twin/test_serial_command_twin.cpp:492-515+ (test_drift_net_console_esp32_only_nrf52_ignores_it), compiled per-side via HAS_NET_CONSOLE
recommendation: Keep split, guarded by DISABLE_NET_CONSOLE as the audit recommended -- the net console depends on net_console.h's TCP server, an ESP32/network-stack feature; porting it to nRF52 is a feature request, not a bug fix.

pair: s_meshcom_settings field parity
esp32_behaviour: Struct (src/esp32/esp32_flash.h:8+) carries, among others, node_disp_rot, node_ntp, node_map, node_audio_start/node_audio_msg (String), node_keyboardlock/node_backlightlock/node_kbllightlock/node_modus/node_mute (T-Deck keyboard/backlight/audio UI state), node_persist_to_flash/node_persist_to_sd/node_immediate_save/node_kbl_sync/node_wifion -- 14 fields not present on nRF52 (esp32_flash.h:70,205,225-239).
nrf52_behaviour: Struct (src/nrf52/WisBlock-API.h:178+) lacks all 14 of the above, and additionally carries two fields ESP32 lacks: send_repeat_time and auto_join (LoRaWAN OTAA join state, WisBlock-API.h near the node_opwd/node_hamnet_only region).
evidence: Direct field-name diff of src/esp32/esp32_flash.h vs. src/nrf52/WisBlock-API.h (both structs read in full 2026-09-12). No U4 twin test exists yet -- test/test_settings_layout, test/test_settings_nvs_keys and test/test_settings_schema_complete (named in testplan-dry-unification-20260910.md section 5.1's table) are not present under test/ today -- source-sourced, not test-sourced.
recommendation: AUDIT UNDERCOUNT, ESCALATE: the pre-filled row said 'six fields missing on nRF52'; the actual diff today is 14 ESP32-only + 2 nRF52-only. Most of the 14 (keyboard/backlight/audio/mute) are T-Deck-hardware-specific UI state with no nRF52 counterpart hardware and are correctly platform-only; node_disp_rot (display rotation) and node_ntp (NTP server string) look general-purpose and worth an explicit per-field decision rather than a blanket 'append all' migration. send_repeat_time/auto_join (nRF52-only) look ESP32-missing for the mirror reason (LoRaWAN OTAA is nRF52-only in this codebase). Needs a field-by-field HITL pass, not a single verdict.

pair: flash-format migration ("compat struct")
esp32_behaviour: No compat-struct migration path exists in the ESP32 flash loader at all -- grep for MESHCOM_COMPAT_MARKER / s_meshcomcompat_settings over src/esp32/ finds no match; ESP32 has never carried an old-format migration struct in this codebase.
nrf52_behaviour: s_meshcomcompat_settings (MESHCOM_COMPAT_MARKER = 0x57) is defined at src/nrf52/WisBlock-API.h:412-413 and used by init_flash() to detect and field-by-field merge an old-layout file into the live struct (src/nrf52/nrf52_flash.cpp:118-140+); every new field added to s_meshcom_settings since the compat struct was frozen must also be added to the merge code by hand, or a migrating device silently loses that field's persisted value.
evidence: src/nrf52/WisBlock-API.h:407-413; src/nrf52/nrf52_flash.cpp:97-140. No U4 twin/lint test exists yet to catch drift between the compat struct and the live one -- source-sourced.
recommendation: Matches the audit's own verdict (both-new): neither ESP32's no-migration-at-all approach nor nRF52's hand-maintained compat struct is the target shape. This is the OPT-07/keyed-settings-store work already tracked in docs/BACKLOG.md (~line 4051, 4286-4394) -- link this row to that backlog item rather than resolving it standalone.

pair: C4 gateway TX pass -- per-loop-pass UDP-out drain trigger
esp32_behaviour: gatewayService_esp32() calls getMeshComUDP() then unconditionally sendMeshComUDP() on every pass where bGATEWAY && node_hasIPaddress, regardless of whether a packet was received this pass (src/esp32/gateway_service_esp32.cpp:20-22).
nrf52_behaviour: gatewayService_nrf52() only calls sendUDP() inside the branch where neth.getUDP()==1 (i.e. NO packet was received this pass); when a packet WAS received, the else branch sets bUDPReceived=true and sendUDP() is skipped entirely for that pass (src/nrf52/gateway_service_nrf52.cpp:32-38).
evidence: src/esp32/gateway_service_esp32.cpp:20-22 vs. src/nrf52/gateway_service_nrf52.cpp:22-45. No twin test exists for gatewayService_*() (not one of the six required suites; C4 is a carve-out, not yet characterized by a U-suite) -- source-sourced.
recommendation: Matches audit: nRF52's TX drain can starve behind a busy RX pass (every receiving pass skips the send this iteration); ESP32's structure -- drain regardless of RX -- looks correct. Implement only after DR-09 is resolved (audit's own dependency note) or as a standalone fix with a soak test, since it changes gateway TX latency under load.

pair: C4 recovery nesting -- connectivity-recovery relative to hasIPaddress
esp32_behaviour: Heartbeat-staleness recovery (Stage 1/Stage 2, resetMeshComUDP()) runs inside `if(bGATEWAY && meshcom_settings.node_hasIPaddress)` (src/esp32/gateway_service_esp32.cpp:20,25-73) -- i.e. WHILE the node believes it still has an IP, specifically to catch a connection that looks up but has gone silent.
nrf52_behaviour: The DHCP/fixIP recovery call (initethfixIP()/resetDHCP()) is reached only inside `if(!neth.hasIPaddress)` (src/nrf52/gateway_service_nrf52.cpp:52-98, guard at :66) -- only after the node has already concluded it does NOT have an IP; no nRF52 path resets a connection that still LOOKS up but has gone silent the way ESP32's Stage 1/2 does.
evidence: src/esp32/gateway_service_esp32.cpp:20-73 vs. src/nrf52/gateway_service_nrf52.cpp:51-102. No twin test exists (same C4 scope as DR-14) -- source-sourced.
recommendation: Same condition and same caveat as DR-14 per the audit: implement together, since both concern how/when each gateway loop notices and recovers from a dead-but-still-up connection.

pair: telemetry/hey trickle-timer gating (bHeyFirst/bTeleFirst/bAllStarted) -- main loop, not gateway_service.h itself
esp32_behaviour: Separate bHeyFirst and bTeleFirst flags, each additionally gated on bAllStarted (src/esp32/esp32_main.cpp:238-241); hey trickle: `(...>= trickle_interval_ms + extra_hey_time) || (bHeyFirst && bAllStarted)` (:3421); telemetry: `(...>= akt_timer) || (bTeleFirst && bAllStarted)` (:3474). extra_hey_time (:3417-3419) adds a 10-minute grace window on one path.
nrf52_behaviour: Only bHeyFirst exists (src/nrf52/nrf52_main.cpp:267); both the hey gate (:1972) and the telemetry gate (:2016) test the SAME bHeyFirst flag -- there is no bTeleFirst, no bAllStarted, and no extra_hey_time on nRF52.
evidence: src/esp32/esp32_main.cpp:238-241,3417-3421,3474-3476 vs. src/nrf52/nrf52_main.cpp:267,1972-1974,2016-2018 (grep confirms zero matches for bTeleFirst/bAllStarted/extra_hey_time under src/nrf52/). No twin test exists -- source-sourced. DEVIATION: this code lives in esp32_main.cpp/nrf52_main.cpp's main loop, not in gateway_service_{esp32,nrf52}.cpp -- the audit's own 'C4' label for this row does not match the C4 carve-out's actual file scope.
recommendation: nRF52's telemetry gate reusing bHeyFirst instead of a dedicated bTeleFirst flag looks like a real bug, not just a missing feature: once the hey trickle has fired once (bHeyFirst cleared), the telemetry 'first send' fast-path is also gone, potentially delaying the first telemetry send by a full akt_timer interval. Port bTeleFirst/bAllStarted/extra_hey_time to nRF52.

pair: countryProfile() per-country radio parameters
esp32_behaviour: Values in MHz (double), bandwidth in kHz (float), coding rate as a 4/N denominator (int) -- e.g. code 0: freq=433.174988 bw=250.0 cr=6 (test/golden/native/country-profile-esp32.txt:4).
nrf52_behaviour: Same physical values in Hz (float), bandwidth as a chip bandwidth-index (0/1/...), coding rate as a chip CR-index -- e.g. code 0: freq=433175008.000000 bw=1.0 cr=2 (test/golden/native/country-profile-nrf52.txt:4).
evidence: test/test_country_twin/test_country_twin.cpp (test_table_matches_the_committed_baseline) against the two committed baselines test/golden/native/country-profile-{esp32,nrf52}.txt, all 17 codes (0-16) compared row-by-row 2026-09-12: every value converts consistently (Hz/1e6 ~= MHz within float rounding; bandwidth/CR index mappings consistent across all 17 codes; preamble identical on both sides for every code). No residual difference beyond the documented unit/API split (OPT-D14) was found.
recommendation: MEASURED, confirms the audit's expectation: keep-split. No further action -- the two representations are the same radio configuration expressed in each platform's own chip-driver units, not a drift to resolve.

pair: EXTUDP forward gate -- before vs. after the recognised-msg_type_b check
esp32_behaviour: sendExtern() to EXTUDP happens INSIDE the `if(msg_type_b == 0x3A || 0x21 || 0x40)` branch (src/esp32/udp_frame_esp32.cpp:98-112) -- a GATE frame with an unrecognised msg_type never reaches sendExtern() at all.
nrf52_behaviour: sendExtern() happens BEFORE that check, unconditionally for every GATE frame (src/nrf52/udp_frame_nrf52.cpp:98-99; the msg_type_b switch is at :102-110) -- an unrecognised msg_type is still forwarded to EXTUDP.
evidence: test/test_udp_frame_twin/test_udp_frame_twin.cpp:738-774 (test_drift_extudp_gate_before_vs_after_msgtype_check)
recommendation: Not in the original audit table -- new finding from the U1 twin. Decide whether forwarding unrecognised-type GATE frames to EXTUDP is desired; if not (matching ESP32), move nRF52's sendExtern() call inside the recognised-type branch.

pair: EXTUDP forward length argument type
esp32_behaviour: Passes lora_tx_msg_len (uint16_t) unchanged to sendExtern() (src/esp32/udp_frame_esp32.cpp:111).
nrf52_behaviour: Casts to (uint8_t) before the call: sendExtern(true, ..., (uint8_t)neth.lora_tx_msg_len, ...) (src/nrf52/udp_frame_nrf52.cpp:99).
evidence: test/test_udp_frame_twin/test_udp_frame_twin.cpp:776-819 (test_drift_extudp_length_arg_type_differs_but_is_unobservable_at_the_clamp) -- the test's own MEASURED LIMIT note: both handlers clamp lora_tx_msg_len to UDP_TX_BUF_SIZE (255) before this call, and 255==UINT8_MAX, so the cast is a no-op today; the risk is latent, live only if UDP_TX_BUF_SIZE is ever raised past 255.
recommendation: Not in the original audit table -- new, currently-inert finding from the U1 twin. No action needed now; re-check if/when UDP_TX_BUF_SIZE is ever raised above 255 (nRF52's cast would start silently truncating where ESP32's would not).

pair: too-many-zeros reject path -- return value and reset call
esp32_behaviour: Returns void; calls resetMeshComUDP() itself on the reject path (src/esp32/udp_frame_esp32.cpp:466-471).
nrf52_behaviour: Returns 1 (too many zeros) and calls no reset itself -- the caller (sendUDP()/gateway loop) is documented to reset DHCP instead (src/nrf52/udp_frame_nrf52.cpp:456,458; doc comment :35-41).
evidence: test/test_udp_frame_twin/test_udp_frame_twin.cpp:938-964 (test_drift_max_zeros_return_value_and_reset_call_differ); also documented as a deliberate, not-yet-decided difference in src/udp_frame.h:33-34
recommendation: Not in the original audit table as its own row (DR-01 covered only the read-BOUND bug, since fixed; this is a separate, still-open difference in what happens on reject). Each side's reset target matches its own connectivity model (ESP32 resets UDP socket state, nRF52's caller resets DHCP) -- decide whether unifying the return-value contract is worth doing on its own, independent of which reset each platform performs.

pair: preconditions before the UDP-out drain runs at all
esp32_behaviour: sendMeshComUDP() refuses to drain in three cases, each an early return: bWIFIAP (AP mode), !hasIPaddress, and node_hostip==0 (unresolved server address) (src/esp32/udp_drain_esp32.cpp:28-35).
nrf52_behaviour: sendUDP() has no equivalent early return for any of the three conditions -- it enters the drain and lets NrfETH::sendUDP() simply fail if the link is not actually usable (src/nrf52/udp_drain_nrf52.cpp:23-25, drain starts immediately).
evidence: test/test_udp_send_twin/test_udp_send_twin.cpp:439-470 (test_drift_esp32_has_three_preconditions_nrf52_has_none)
recommendation: Port the three ESP32 preconditions (or nRF52's own equivalents) to sendUDP(); draining into a known-bad link wastes a ring slot's worth of processing (decode/print/zero-out) on every pass instead of a cheap early return.

pair: decode-and-print after a failed socket write
esp32_behaviour: Decodes and prints the frame unconditionally, whether or not the write succeeded (src/esp32/udp_drain_esp32.cpp:69-134; the decode/print block at :108-134 is outside the write's if/else).
nrf52_behaviour: Decode/print sits inside the else (success) branch of `if(!neth.sendUDP(...))` (src/nrf52/udp_drain_nrf52.cpp:48-100) -- a failed write means no decode and no print at all for that frame.
evidence: test/test_udp_send_twin/test_udp_send_twin.cpp:472-497 (test_drift_failed_write_decodes_on_esp32_only)
recommendation: Debug-visibility difference only (printBuffer_aprs() has no side effect beyond the log line) -- decide whether a failed-write frame should still be visible in the TX-UDP debug log on nRF52 (matching ESP32) purely for operability, not correctness.

pair: endPacket()-equivalent call after a failed write
esp32_behaviour: Calls udpEndRaw_esp32() unconditionally after the write attempt, unless the error-limit branch already returned (src/esp32/udp_drain_esp32.cpp:92-99, early return at :88).
nrf52_behaviour: No separate end-packet call at this call site -- NrfETH::sendUDP() (src/nrf52/nrf_eth.cpp:338+) is documented to already end the packet itself as part of handling its own failure, so the drain layer does not repeat the call (src/nrf52/udp_drain_nrf52.cpp:48-67).
evidence: test/test_udp_send_twin/test_udp_send_twin.cpp:499-511 (test_drift_esp32_calls_endpacket_after_a_failed_write)
recommendation: Layering difference, not a functional gap -- both sides end the packet, just at different call depths (drain layer vs. inside NrfETH::sendUDP()). No action needed; noted so a future refactor of either layer does not accidentally drop the call on one side.

pair: behaviour at the TX error limit (MAX_ERR_UDP_TX)
esp32_behaviour: On tripping the limit: resets the socket via resetMeshComUDP() and RETURNS BEFORE the ring-read-pointer advance/slot-zero -- the failing slot stays in the ring and is retried on the next pass (src/esp32/udp_drain_esp32.cpp:76-89, early return at :88; advance/zero at :143-155 never reached that pass).
nrf52_behaviour: On tripping the limit: resets DHCP via neth.resetDHCP() but does NOT return -- falls through to the same advance/zero block, so the failing slot is zeroed and dropped, not retried (src/nrf52/udp_drain_nrf52.cpp:56-66 no return; advance/zero at :107-113 runs every pass).
evidence: test/test_udp_send_twin/test_udp_send_twin.cpp:513-560 (test_drift_error_limit_esp32_retries_the_slot_nrf52_drops_it) -- the test's own comment calls this 'the sharpest difference in the pair'
recommendation: Real functional divergence with opposite failure modes: ESP32 can wedge forever retrying one permanently-failing slot (head-of-line block on the ring), nRF52 silently drops one frame per socket reset. Needs a HITL correctness call, not a default 'ESP32' port -- neither behaviour is obviously right.

pair: RX-01 unconfigured-source guard on the OUTBOUND UDP-to-server drain (second door -- the frame has already been sent by this point on both sides)
esp32_behaviour: Counts and suppresses the debug print for a decoded frame whose APRS source is still the factory callsign via logRxDropUnconfigured(), AFTER the UDP send has already happened (src/esp32/udp_drain_esp32.cpp:117-133).
nrf52_behaviour: No such check anywhere in sendUDP() (src/nrf52/udp_drain_nrf52.cpp) -- an unconfigured-source frame is sent and printed exactly like any other.
evidence: test/test_udp_send_twin/test_udp_send_twin.cpp:562-593 (test_drift_rx01_unconfigured_guard_is_esp32_only) -- a DIFFERENT call site from DR-02 (this is the outbound drain's own copy of the same RX-01 idea, not the inbound frame handler)
recommendation: Same family as DR-02 but a separate call site -- port for consistent RX-01 accounting/log suppression across both of nRF52's UDP paths, not just the inbound one.

pair: debug-print prefix text for a relayed TX-UDP frame
esp32_behaviour: One fixed prefix, "TX-UDP " (single trailing space); never reads bDisplayVia (src/esp32/udp_drain_esp32.cpp:132).
nrf52_behaviour: bDisplayVia selects between "[MESHu]...TX-UDP  " (two trailing spaces) and "TX-UDP  " (also two trailing spaces, differing from ESP32's one) (src/nrf52/udp_drain_nrf52.cpp:89-99).
evidence: test/test_udp_send_twin/test_udp_send_twin.cpp:595-617 (test_drift_nrf52_prefixes_the_print_with_mesh_when_via_is_on)
recommendation: Display-log text only, no functional effect. Low priority; unify the trailing-space count and decide whether bDisplayVia's extra prefix is worth porting to ESP32 for log-parsing consistency.

pair: encodeAPRS()/decodeAPRS() epilogue SUB-byte round trip (SHARED code -- src/aprs_functions.cpp is one file linked into both firmware images; no ESP32-vs-nRF52 split for this row) [OPT-D15]
esp32_behaviour: Same as nRF52 -- shared implementation. Encoder substitutes SUB=0x00 with 0x23 ('#') but writes SUB=0x7E VERBATIM (src/aprs_functions.cpp:1356-1359), producing two consecutive 0x7E bytes on the wire when a node's sub-version is literally 0x7E ('~').
nrf52_behaviour: Same as ESP32 -- shared implementation. Decoder reads the first 0x7E of that pair back as '#' (src/aprs_functions.cpp:469-473) and separately consumes the second 0x7E as the frame terminator: a node whose sub-version is 0x7E silently becomes '#' after one hop, on any receiver, regardless of platform.
evidence: docs/BACKLOG.md OPT-D15 (~line 4612); test/test_aprs_epilogue/test_aprs_epilogue.cpp:298-316 (test_epilogue_sub_0x7e_collision, 4/4 mutations caught per the backlog entry)
recommendation: Not a cross-platform drift (both platforms share this bug identically) -- carried into this matrix per task instruction. The eventual fix is a single wire-format decision (extend the encoder's substitution to 0x7E, or escape it) applied once to shared code, not a per-platform port. docs/BACKLOG.md flags this as OPEN, pinned not fixed, and a fleet-compatibility question (changing an encoder both ends already agree on) rather than a simple bugfix.

pair: mHeard list display order (SHARED code -- src/mheard_functions.cpp is one file linked into both firmware images) [OPT-D16, part 1]
esp32_behaviour: Same as nRF52 -- shared implementation. showMHeard() is a plain `for(int iset=0; iset<MAX_MHEARD; iset++)` physical-slot walk (src/mheard_functions.cpp:772), not sorted by recency or callsign.
nrf52_behaviour: Same as ESP32 -- shared implementation. sendMheard() (the JSON/BLE serializer) uses the identical physical-slot scan (src/mheard_functions.cpp:694) -- both renderers agree with each other, just not with any notion of 'most recently heard first'.
evidence: docs/BACKLOG.md OPT-D16 (~line 4613); test/test_mheard_render/test_mheard_render.cpp:291-334 (test_showMHeard_zeigt_physische_slot_reihenfolge_nicht_zeit_oder_alphabet -- hearing order C,A,B displays as B,A,C; re-hearing C does not move it) and :450-473 (test_sendMheard_physische_slot_reihenfolge, confirms sendMheard() matches the same physical order)
recommendation: Not a cross-platform drift -- shared code, carried into this matrix per task instruction. docs/BACKLOG.md: sorting by last-heard is the obvious behaviour and cheap (<=80 slots) but changes what every user sees, so it is flagged as a product decision, not a correctness fix.

pair: PLT field representation, showMHeard() vs. sendMheard() (SHARED code) [OPT-D16, part 2]
esp32_behaviour: Same as nRF52 -- shared implementation. showMHeard()'s 'typ' column prints the DECODED text via getPayloadType() -- "TXT"/"POS"/"HEY" (test evidence: golden text "POS"/"TXT" rows in test_mheard_render.cpp).
nrf52_behaviour: Same as ESP32 -- shared implementation. sendMheard()'s JSON "PLT" field is the RAW (uint8_t) ASCII code of the type byte, not the decoded text -- e.g. '!' (0x21) serializes as PLT:33, not "POS" (src/mheard_functions.cpp:742).
evidence: test/test_mheard_render/test_mheard_render.cpp:429-445 (test_sendMheard_ein_frischer_eintrag_json_feldreihenfolge, asserts PLT:33) compared against :262 (showMHeard()'s golden row showing "POS" for the same payload type); comment at :425-428 names the finding explicitly
recommendation: Not a cross-platform drift -- shared code. Two renderers of the same underlying byte disagree on text-vs-numeric representation; harmless for the app (which presumably decodes PLT itself) but worth a single documented contract (is PLT a wire-type byte or a display string?) rather than leaving it implicit.
